On Thu, 15 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -0700 Sofia Ivanova wrote:
> We're looking into this now. Dylan (SRE) is triaging and I'll get an initial status within 30–45 minutes.

Status update:
- No infra deploys in the last 12 hours on the hosted fleet in US-west.
- We've identified a correlated rise in concurrent 32k-context sessions starting ~05:40 UTC; concurrency jumped ~3x from baseline.
- Error type: timeouts while waiting on the model runtime (backend token loop), not upstream network 504s.
- Immediate mitigation applied (10:45 UTC): soft-rate-limit for requests with context >24k and enable model-variant fallback for calls that accept a compatible shorter-window model.

What we're doing next:
1) Rolling a hot patch to isolate long-window execution to a smaller pool (quarantine nodes) to prevent head-of-line blocking. ETA 45m.
2) Capturing trace samples and KV cache hit rates.
3) If quota of dedicated long-window capacity exceeded, we will auto-fallback to the 16k variant and mark requests in logs.

Ask for Meridian: please confirm that fallback to 16k is acceptable temporarily and whether any requests require guaranteed 32k fidelity.

Dylan

Subject: Re: Increased timeouts and p99 spikes for long-window endpoints

Folks —

Preliminary engineering notes (root-cause hypothesis):
- Symptom: p99 spike and timeouts on high-concurrency long-context requests.
- Likely cause: contention in the KV cache and increased per-request memory pressure when many 32k sessions are pinned to general-purpose nodes. Long-window requests increase KV miss rates and force repeated expensive attention/tensor ops; under concurrency this pushes runtime into long tail.

Short-term actions (now–4 hours):
1) Quarantine long-window traffic to isolated GPU pool (applied) to limit interference with other tenants.
2) Reduce max concurrent long-window handoffs per node from 8 -> 3.
3) Enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for repeat prompts from Meridian (cache keying using customer id + prompt hash).
4) Provide explicit logs/trace IDs for any fallback events and attach p99_trend_07-15.png to the Jira.

Medium-term (72 hours):
- Increase long-window capacity (provision more nodes with higher memory), fine-tune kernel selection for 32k execution path, and add prioritized queueing for jobs that flagged as "must preserve 32k".

I'll follow up with a short post-mortem once we have full traces.

-Markus
Director, Runtime Engineering

Subject: Exec summary: Meridian long-window p99/timeouts — containment & next steps

Quick executive summary for visibility:

What happened
- Meridian Analytics experienced increased p99 latency (up to 60s) and ~12% timeouts on 32k-context hosted API calls during a concurrency spike on 2026-07-15. Root cause appears to be runtime contention for long-window workloads on general-purpose nodes.

Containment completed
- SRE quarantined long-window traffic to a limited GPU pool and applied soft rate-limits and fallbacks to 16k where acceptable.
- Engineering applied immediate changes to per-node concurrency and enabled aggressive prefix caching for Meridian.

Customer impact and ask
- Meridian accepts temporary 16k fallback for most jobs; two nightly pipelines requested preserved 32k — they will supply job IDs for whitelisting.
- We should consider offering a short usage credit and follow-up post-mortem to maintain relationship.

Next steps (owners)
- Dylan: capture full traces and confirm whether any recoverable errors occurred (ETA 6h).
- Markus: capacity plan for long-window fleet and prioritized queueing (ETA 72h).
- Sofia/Stephanie: coordinate customer comms and credit request (ETA EOB today).

I'll escalate to CTO if we see repeated incidents in the next 7 days.

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Reliability
